svg.font-family: ui-sans-serif, -apple-system, 'Segoe UI', Roboto, 'Helvetica Neue', Arial, sans-serif
svg.title: Walk-forward validation versus shuffled cross-validation
svg.desc: Shuffled K-fold places training samples after the test fold in time, so the model is fitted on the future. Walk-forward keeps every training sample before its test window, with a purge gap for the label horizon and an embargo for serial correlation.
svg.text: Same data, same model, opposite meaning
Training samples sit on BOTH sides of every test sample. The model interpolates between known points
instead of extrapolating into an unknown future. Accuracy goes up. Profit does not.
train: strictly before the test window
purge: dropped, its labels overlap the test period
Stitching the test windows together gives one continuous out-of-sample equity curve.
That curve is the only performance number in this workshop that counts as evidence.
